recommendations: ACHD patients with chronic HF should be referred to specialized centres.
Specific guidelines for medical treatment of chronic HF in ACHD are lacking; practitioners should follow current guidelines for medical treatment of HF.
Sacubitril/valsartan may decrease morbidity, however no recommendation can be made at this moment based on retrospective or anecdotal observations.
Co-morbidities in HF such as diabetes mellitus, AF, CSA, iron deficiency, and cachexia should be treated according to specific recommendations in this document.

In a biventricular circulation, patients with an impaired systemic LV should be treated with conventional HF therapy; this may also be considered in symptomatic patients with a failing systemic right ventricle.
Diuretics are recommended to control symptoms of fluid retention.

Treatment of symptomatic patients with a failing single ventricle in a Fontan circulation, or with a persistent right-to-left shunt, should be carefully initiated taking ventricular preload and systemic afterload into account.

CRT may be a therapeutic option in ACHD patients with HF, but evidence in this setting is lacking; efficacy depends on underlying structural and functional substrate (ventricle anatomy, AV valve regurgitation, myocardial scarring, conduction delay).
Treatment of acute HF in ACHD patients should be in an expert centre with knowledge of inotropes, availability of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and advanced bridging techniques.
Timely evaluation for transplantation by ACHD HF specialists in a transplant centre with ACHD expertise is recommended.
Ventricular assist devices can bridge patients to transplantation or, in a subgroup, be used as destination therapy.
therapies_and_interventions: conventional HF therapy for systemic LV dysfunction
careful management for failing single ventricle/Fontan patients
CRT (cardiac resynchronization therapy) — potential option but evidence lacking in ACHD
inotropes and ECMO in expert centres for acute HF
clinical_practice_notes: Evidence for some interventions in ACHD HF is limited and often retrospective or anecdotal; clinical decisions should consider underlying anatomy and individual risks/benefits.
Management of ACHD HF often requires specialized centres with ACHD expertise and advanced support options.
page_observations: Several recommendations and statements are repeated within the page (sacubitril/valsartan note and core management principles appear more than once).
